Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the HealthBridge Hospitals Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold as it may be automatically removed from the conference. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HealthBridge Hospitals Inc.'s financial results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and David Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the Q3 2024. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on four key aspects: capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion, factors affecting operating margin such as revenue growth and cost control, operating margin by segment, and breakdown of revenue by service line.

These areas highlight our progress in strengthening our 42-hospital footprint and outpatient network amid favorable industry dynamics like increasing procedure volumes and value-based care adoption. Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa to provide a more detailed review of our financial results, including deep dives into these aspects.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the Q3 2024 was $2.75 billion, an increase of 8.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable case mix shifts, and strong performance in our outpatient channels. Our operating expenses were $2.40 billion, representing 87.3% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives.

Net income for the quarter was $215 million, or $1.38 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

To give you more insight into the drivers behind these results, let me start with our capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion, which totaled $285 million in Q3. This marks an 18% increase year-over-year and sits at the high end of our full-year guidance of $1.05 to $1.15 billion. This investment reflects our disciplined yet aggressive approach to boosting operational efficiency, increasing patient throughput, and gaining market share in high-growth areas, supported by trends such as rising procedure volumes and site-neutral reimbursement policies.

Breaking it down, about 62% or $177 million went toward modernizing our existing 42-hospital network, while 38% supported expansion efforts. Year-to-date, modernization spending is running 12% ahead of 2023, addressing our portfolio's average age of 25 years and incorporating cutting-edge clinical technologies to advance value-based care.

Key modernization priorities included a $120 million multi-year Epic MyChart electronic health record optimization across 28 facilities, with Q3 marking Phase II go-lives in our Southeast region. This has cut clinician documentation time by 14%, similar to outcomes at HCA Healthcare after their Epic implementations, and sets us up for compliance with the CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule. We also allocated $45 million to advanced imaging and procedural suites, featuring three Siemens MAGNETOM Free.Max 0.55T MRIs and two GE Optima CT scanners for low-dose cardiac imaging. These have shortened scan times by 20-25%, lifting our outpatient imaging to 42% of radiology revenues from 35% last year, helping us stand strong against freestanding imaging providers. Additionally, $32 million enhanced our operating rooms with four new Intuitive Surgical da Vinci Xi systems and Stryker Mako robotic arms for orthopedics. In the Midwest, these changes reduced average length of stay by 0.8 days for joint replacements, boosting our case mix index by 9% to 1.72.

These efforts are customized by region. In the Sunbelt, home to 55% of our beds in Florida, Texas, and the Carolinas, we're upgrading for high-acuity care to match Medicare Advantage growth to 42% of our payer mix, up 500 basis points year-over-year. For example, our Tampa Bay campus got $18 million for a hybrid OR suite to handle complex endovascular procedures demanded by aging Boomers. In rural Midwest sites like Iowa and Nebraska, $22 million funded tele-ICU expansions with Philips eICU, easing physician shortages and dropping sepsis mortality by 15%, aligning with Leapfrog Group standards.

On expansion, our $108 million Q3 outlay rose 22% year-over-year, aimed at new capacity and small acquisitions for 4-6% same-facility growth. We've started construction on a 120-bed acute-care hospital in Dallas-Fort Worth, a $250 million initiative funded by our $1.2 billion revolver, opening Q4 2025 with 15 extra ORs to grab 12% market share amid ASC builds by HCA and Tenet. We're also developing six micro-hospitals totaling 240 beds in outer Texas and Georgia areas, ED-focused at $35 million apiece, expected to hit 18-20% EBITDA margins in two years—better than full hospitals—and tapping a 7% CAGR in ED visits per CDC figures.

These investments target throughput gains amid 11% year-over-year elective surgery growth post-COVID, resilience to labor issues with 8% fewer RN hours per patient day via automation, and readiness for CMS OPPS cuts through cost savings offsetting 2-3% reimbursement pressures. ROIC on 2023 projects is at 14%, beating our 12% threshold, with FY24 CapEx set to add $180 million in EBITDA by 2026 via volumes and margins.

For 2025, we're adding $150 million including Trane HVAC retrofits for ESG compliance and 15% energy savings. This keeps HealthBridge leading in consolidation, following Universal Health Services' ambulatory strategy.

Next, let's discuss the factors affecting our operating margin, which reached 12.5% this quarter—a 130 basis point expansion from 11.2% last year and our best since pre-pandemic times. This beat our guidance midpoint of 11.5% to 12.5%, thanks to strong revenue growth and tight cost controls despite labor inflation and supply disruptions.

Revenue growth of 8.2% year-over-year to $2.75 billion, with 7.1% same-facility, was the main driver, from 4.5% more patient days and 2.6% higher net revenue per patient day. Admissions rose 3.8%, inpatient to 95% of 2019 levels, outpatient up 12% via ASCs and imaging. CMI grew 1.8% to 1.92 on ortho and cardio procedures with better DRG pay under CMS IPPS.

Payer mix improved: commercial at 52% from 49%, especially Southeast employer plans. Medicare revenue per admission up 4.2% to $14,200 with 2.9% inpatient hikes and 85% MSSP quality scores. Medicaid dipped 2% Midwest from redeterminations in Ohio and Michigan, offset by 5-7% better commercial rates.

Southeast grew 10% like HCA, from Florida/Texas electives; Northeast 5% softer from flu and site-neutral issues like Community Health Systems. We're diversifying via Optum value-based cardiology ($45 million gain) and GLP-1 protocols (15% ancillary boost). Q4 revenue per day flat to +1% with robotic surgery CMI gains.

Costs grew 5.8%, delivering 240 basis points leverage. SG&A fell 80 basis points to 4.9% post-Oracle Cerner EHR at 75% of footprint.

Labor (52% expenses) up 6.2% but slowing from Q2's 8%, RN inflation at 4.5% vs. 6-7% industry via $150 million workforce program with nursing schools like Tenet. Travelers under 5% from 12%, premium pay 3.2% from 5.1%.

Supplies up 3.1% vs. 7% inflation, Vizient GPO 12% ortho/8% stent savings, 15% SKU cuts ($28 million save), flat pharmacy via auth on gene therapies/biosimilars despite GLP-1s.

Tech: Change Healthcare AI cut AR days to 45, Epic analytics no-shows 18%. Capex 4.2% revenue on tele-ICU (11% utilization).

West strongest (320bps expansion) via utilities/California Medicaid; Midwest 100bps from unions.

We guide FY24 margins 12.0-12.8% from prior, 6-7% revenue, 4% labor taper. Risks: 0.3% IPPS cut FY25, Medicaid extensions; offsets: 20% ASC revenue by 2026, MSSP.

This balance—acuity/outpatient top-line, tech/supply bottom-line—lifts ROIC to 11.2%, competitive with UHS.

Moving to operating margin by segment, our diversified model shines with consolidated 7.2%—up 110 basis points year-over-year, 40 sequentially, best post-pandemic. Acute hospitals, ASCs, behavioral health, and physician services buffered challenges.

Acute care hospitals (76% revenue, 42 sites in 12 states, Sunbelt focus): 4.8% margin, +160bps YoY highest in 3 years. $2.1 billion revenue +5.2%, 3.8% admissions, CMI +110bps to 1.92 on ortho/cardio. Labor +4.1% via CareForward (25% traveler drop, AMN pipelines). Supplies +2.7%, HealthTrust $45M savings on implants. Sunbelt +220bps over Northeast, Texas 6.2% on 7% volumes vs. Pennsylvania flat. FY24 IPPS tailwind, AI revenue cycle (Epic/Nuance DAX) denial -15%, +50bps 2024.

ASCs (12% revenue, 150 sites incl. USPI JVs): 28.4% margin, +90bps sequential. $420M +12.5%, 10% procedures (spine/GI), site-neutral 40-50% > HOPD. ASC Excellence: sterile hubs -8% supplies, 15% hospital shift ($100M). Dallas/Phoenix 85% utilization >72% VMG. 3 de novo Q1 2024 +200bps.

Behavioral health (8% revenue, 35 freestanding/20 units): 12.1% -70bps YoY on LOS pushback, +50bps sequential. $280M +8.3%, 6% admissions (IOP/PHP post-parity). Medicaid unwind 22% mix, offset commercial +4.5%. Telepsych 35% encounters (Talkspace) -12% RN hours. Southeast Florida 14.2%, Midwest cuts. MindCore apps 40% beds, +100bps 2024.

Physician services (4% revenue, 2,500 providers): 15.6% +140bps, $140M +9% encounters/RVUs (athenahealth). ScribeAmerica -20% admin, 25% cross-referrals.

Diversification (ASC/behavioral to 22%) like HCA/Tenet buffers acute. FY consolidated 7.0-7.5%, $150M savings (Vizient AI, ShiftMed, ACO REACH). $1.2B M&A outpatient, 8-10% margins 2025. Risks: wages, IRA drugs.

Finally, the breakdown of revenue by service line shows our shift to outpatient/procedural. Total net patient service revenues $2.75 billion, +5.2% YoY or 3.8% same-facility ex-divestitures of 3 rural Midwest hospitals.

Inpatient acute care: 42% or $1.16 billion, down from 45% mix. Admissions +1.1%, rev/admission +0.9% to $14,250, Medicare CMI -2.3% IPPS. +2.0% YoY, Sunbelt 4% (45% commercial Texas/Florida like HCA), Midwest flat Medicaid post-redeterms. ApexFlow AI -0.4 days ALOS, mid-single CMI H2.

Outpatient services: 30% $825 million +14.2%, +60bps margin to 22%. Clinic/infusion/imaging volumes +16%, 120 physician clinics/USPI JVs. Site-neutral/NO Surprises, Southeast 55% volume >Tenet 52%. $45M Epic telehealth +28% to 150k visits (8%), rural KY/TN.

Emergency department: 13% $358 million flat YoY. Visits +2.5% to 1.26M, rev/visit -2.4% to $285 (payer scrutiny). ED Surge AI -15% boarding to <4hrs like UHS, LWBS 1.8%. Urban Atlanta/Dallas +5% trauma.

Surgical services (35 ASCs): 10% $275 million +9.8%. Procedures +12%, $8,200/case ortho/cardio (TAVR/spine) shift. 5 new ASCs Q3, 20% EBITDA vs 15% hospital, 55% commercial like CHS.

Behavioral health: 3% $83 million +18%, discharges +22% to 47k, 92% occupancy 15 facilities. Acuity pricing Blue Cross like Acadia.

Ancillary (labs/imaging/home): 2% $55 million +6%, 4D AI MRI.

Summary: inpatient 42% $1.16B +2%, outpatient 30% $825M +14.2%, ED 13% $358M flat, surgical 10% $275M +9.8%, behavioral 3% $83M +18%, ancillary 2% $55M +6%, total $2.75B +5.2%.

Outpatient to 35% year-end via $200M ASC/clinic capex. Payer rates +3-4%, R1 RCM denials 1.2%. Labor 52% risk, FY25 IPPS cuts, but diversified like peers.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Lisa. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of Medicare Advantage penetration on your operations?

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Good morning, Emily. Absolutely. As Lisa detailed, Medicare Advantage now represents 42% of our payer mix, up 500 basis points year-over-year, particularly in Sunbelt markets. We've tailored our investments—like high-acuity OR upgrades in Tampa Bay and tele-ICU in rural Midwest—to handle this shift, enabling complex procedures and improving outcomes such as 15% better sepsis rates. This supports our value-based care push through MSSP and ACOs, where we're scoring 85% on quality, helping offset any utilization pressures while driving CMI to 1.92.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline:
Thanks. What are your expectations for patient volume growth in the next quarter, considering the current environment?

Lisa Chen:
Hi Robert. We're guiding for 4-5% same-facility patient volume growth in Q4, building on this quarter's 4.5% patient days increase. This assumes continued rebound in electives (11% YoY trend), 10-12% outpatient surges from ASCs and imaging, and ED CAGR of 7%. Tailwinds include robotic OR expansions reducing ALOS and AI tools cutting no-shows 18%, though we're monitoring seasonal factors and Medicaid redeterminations. CMI gains from ortho/cardio should support flat to +1% revenue per day.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks for taking my question. On the expansion side, can you elaborate on the micro-hospital strategy and expected returns?

Lisa Chen:
Sure, Alex. Our six micro-hospitals totaling 240 beds in exurban Texas and Georgia are ED-driven, $35 million each, projecting 18-20% EBITDA margins within 24 months—outpacing traditional builds. They're responding to ED volume growth and ASC competition, adding capacity like the DFW 120-bed hospital. Early ROIC on similar projects is 14%, above our 12% hurdle, with full ramp generating incremental EBITDA through higher throughput and efficiencies.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session. I'll now turn the call back over to Dr. Reynolds for closing remarks.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the HealthBridge Hospitals Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
